providers.name: University of Toledo College of Engineering — K-12 Outreach
providers.description: Year-round K-12 engineering outreach. The Robotic Rubik's Cube Challenge sets up school Mechatronics Clubs (with Dana, Owens Community College and Toledo Public Schools, NSF-funded) with twice-weekly after-school online training in electronics, coding and robotics, reduced to weekly after the first semester; UToledo supplies Siemens PLC software, electronic kits, motors, controllers and curriculum. The page lists club starts for Jan. 2024 and Sept. 2025, 2026 and 2027 (re-confirmed 2026-08-24). Also runs the Introduce a Girl to Engineering series — from 2026 these events are open to middle school boys and girls, not girls only — and the PEER high-school research program, which places pre-college students with engineering faculty researchers. RE-CHECK 2026-08-31: the page is unchanged and still advertises the Introduce a Girl to Engineering dates of February 27 and March 20, 2026 — both now past — with no 2026–27 replacement dates published. Mechatronics Club starts are still listed for September 2026 and September 2027. Phone 419-530-8040 and EnUGStudies@utoledo.edu re-confirmed.

providers.name: Owens Community College / Kool Kat Science
providers.description: Kool Kat Science (a.k.a. Pandaia Projects) runs project-based youth STEM classes and camps through Owens' Workforce & Community Services and at partner sites. Owens' current Kids & Teens catalog lists ~33 courses, including 'Coding with Scratch Jr.' (ages 6–8) and 'AI & Machine Learning' (ages 9–12), plus robotics, 3D printing and science titles, mostly for ages 5–12 — but Owens publishes no dates or prices on the catalog listing page, so call for both. CONFIRMED for 2026–27 (Kool Kat's own site, 2026-08-17): the organization won the City of Toledo Youth Programming Grant for a third year, and is launching Future Builders Lab — a 15-week afterschool program for grades 3–6 with New Leaf Group, built from three five-week mini-courses (Rookie Makers, Rookie Coders, Rookie Robotics) plus help with STEM magnet high-school applications — in fall 2026. It also runs STEM in the Stacks at the library (see the Toledo Lucas County Public Library entry), a Micro:bit Maker Lab at Toledo Tech Loft downtown, and South City STEAM at Mosaic Family Zone on Orchard Street in the Old South End (City-sponsored 5-day camps at $20, fully refunded as a gift card for full attendance; camps include Kibble Caper Forensics and Forces of Nature for ages 6–8 and Mechanical Puppet and Rookie Robotics for ages 9–12). CAUTION on South City STEAM: Kool Kat's page for it is titled 2025 while the announcing blog post is dated April 14, 2026, and no specific camp dates are published — confirm the year and dates before referring families. RE-CHECK 2026-08-24: the Owens Kids & Teens catalog now lists 34 youth courses (ages 5–12) plus separate teen courses, and koolkatscience.net redirects to koolkatscience.org. CORRECTION 2026-08-31: 'Future Builders Lab' IS confirmed after all — it is described on Kool Kat's own Milestones & Momentum page (koolkatscience.org/milestones-momentum/), which last week's check missed: a 15-week fall-2026 afterschool programme for grades 3–6 run with New Leaf Group, built from three five-week mini-courses (Rookie Makers, Rookie Coders, Rookie Robotics), funded by a $10,000 Toledo Rotary Club Foundation grant and including help with STEM magnet high-school applications. The same page confirms STEM in the Stacks (16 weeks, TLCPL Heatherdowns branch, Toledo Youth Programming Grant 2026–27) and adds a previously unrecorded programme: WTPA STEM Enrichment, a 12-week in-school programme for grades 2–4 at Western Toledo Preparatory Academy, on the same Rotary grant. Specific start dates, session times and fees for all three are still unpublished — call before referring families.

location.venue: Owens Workforce & Community Services, 30335 Oregon Rd

providers.season: Year-round. Three fall-2026 programmes confirmed 2026-08-31: Future Builders Lab (grades 3–6, 15 weeks), STEM in the Stacks (TLCPL Heatherdowns, 16 weeks) and WTPA STEM Enrichment (grades 2–4, 12 weeks). No start dates are published for any of them.

providers.name: Imagination Station
providers.description: Downtown science center running week-long summer STEM camps for ages 6–13, plus a sensory-friendly week and monthly school-year homeschool workshops for grades K–8 on select Tuesdays and Wednesdays (separate K–3 and 4–8 sessions on each date). The full 2026–27 homeschool calendar is now published through May 2027. The center also runs recurring 'Think Tank' drop-in workshops, Family Explorers Club sessions and monthly Sensory Friendly Sundays. Workshop pricing is still not published anywhere on the site — call for costs. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-31: the full K–3 / 4–8 monthly homeschool schedule through May 2027 is still posted, and three further Think Tank workshops have been added to the fall calendar (Pumpkin Carving in October, Sew Fun in November, Gingerbread Houses in December). Neither the homeschool workshops nor the Think Tank workshops publish a price on the events calendar or the educators page — cost remains unverified for all of them.
providers.cost: $250/week members, $275/week non-members (summer camps); homeschool workshop and Think Tank pricing not published
